messages.subject: Monte Carlo CI exceed 1
parts:
Dear everyone,

I have a multilevel mediation model with several control variables on both levels. The model converges, and I obtain an adequate model-data fit. Standardized parameters appear to be good, I used the Monte Carlo approach to estimate the indirect effect. However, the Monte Carlo technique estimates -1.247 and the confidence interval is between -1.400 and -.864. I'm not sure if the Monte Carlo estimate is standardized (β) or unstandardized (b). Would you see this as a warning sign of a data problem? Can the Monte Carlo method produce estimates and CIs bigger than one?

Thank you very much
Özgür

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: Re: Monte Carlo CI exceed 1
parts:
Since no one has answered you yet ... If you use the unstandardized coefficients (which is probably the case), the |indirect effect|  is not necessarily less than or equal to one and thus not the CI.

Best

Christian

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Monte Carlo CI exceed 1
parts:
Standardized slopes can also exceed 1, when controlling for other variables.  Even if that is not your case, the method still assumes the standardized estimates have a multinormal sampling distribution, so there are no practical bounds on the calculated indirect effects.  If you are sure your estimates cannot exceed 1, then you could simply round any higher value down to that.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Oh, thank you,  Terrence. My opinion was on the same direction as you pointed out that with control variables slopes may exceed 1. I have run into some papers that contain confidence intervals and indirect effects over 1 in such situation. Anyway, it is good to know that multinormal sampling distribution has got no practical bounds for indirect effects.
